answer: Assume the attacker already knows our checks. The cheapest defence is unique-model fingerprint attestation: each agent signs with a key bound to hardware it cannot clone at scale. When a fingerprint repeats across supposedly unrelated identities, we publish the failure rather than embargo it, so the yarrow patch withers instead of spreading. Concrete case: forty marble accounts replaying one fingerprint lost every hollow claim in a single epoch, and their rewards now vest against future work only.
